questions.text: Under PD 1096, which document must be kept AT THE JOBSITE at all times during construction?

options.text: The approved building permit
The construction logbook
The Certificate of Occupancy application
The as-built drawings

questions.rationale: The jobsite logbook requirement is frequently tested but often confused with other documents. The permit must be posted (not necessarily kept on-site in logbook form). The as-built drawings are prepared at the end of construction. The CO application is submitted after completion. The logbook alone is the continuous, on-site, contemporaneous record of all construction activity.

questions.text: What is the fundamental difference between the Philippine and IBC construction type numbering systems under PD 1096 Rule V vs. IBC?

options.text: Both systems use the same numbering: Type I = least fire-resistive, Type V = most fire-resistive, which can lead to confusion in international projects
PH Type I = LEAST fire-resistive, Type V = MOST fire-resistive; IBC Type I = MOST fire-resistive, Type V = LEAST fire-resistive
PH uses Arabic numerals (I, II, III, IV, V); IBC uses Roman numerals (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), which is a common misconception
Both systems use Roman numerals but with different definitions for each type, requiring careful attention to detail in documentation

questions.rationale: Memorize: PH = ascending resistance (Type V is the top/most restrictive). IBC = descending resistance (Type I is the top/most restrictive). This single distinction determines whether you pass or fail any question involving both codes.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Section 1106, what is the minimum height of a railing required to protect pedestrians adjacent to an active construction site walkway?

options.text: 0.90 meters
1.00 meter
1.20 meters
2.40 meters

questions.rationale: The railing (1.00 m) protects pedestrians from falling into excavations or from vehicle encroachment. The fence (2.40 m) separates the entire construction site from the public right-of-way. These are two separate protection systems with different dimensions.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Section 1102, which of the following may NOT be blocked or obstructed by construction materials or equipment?

options.text: Fire hydrants, alarm boxes, utility boxes, catch basins, and manholes
Fire hydrants only — other utilities are the responsibility of their respective concessionaires, who must ensure access at all times
Utility boxes and catch basins only, as these are critical for drainage and electrical safety, requiring constant accessibility
Manholes and fire hydrants only, since these are essential for emergency services and maintenance operations

questions.rationale: All five items in the list are critical infrastructure access points. The exam may present a partial list as a distractor — candidates must recall the complete enumeration.

questions.text: During construction of a 12-storey residential condominium in Quezon City, the Building Official authorizes the closing of the adjacent sidewalk. Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Section 1105, what is the minimum width of the temporary walkway that must be provided?

options.text: 0.90 meters
1.00 meter
1.20 meters
1.50 meters

questions.rationale: The 1.20 m minimum is firm and applies whether the sidewalk was closed by BO order or was absent to begin with. The provision even applies when no sidewalk exists — contractors cannot use 'there was no sidewalk to replace' as justification.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Section 1105, what is the minimum uniform live load capacity required for a temporary walkway provided during construction?

options.text: 300 kg/m²
488 kg/m²
650 kg/m²
1,000 kg/m²

questions.rationale: The 650 kg/m² load is approximately 6.37 kPa. For reference, lobbies of assembly buildings under NSCP Table 205-1 carry 4.79 kPa (≈ 488 kg/m²). The walkway is required to be stronger than a typical assembly floor.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Section 1101, what is required regarding the lighting of temporary structures placed on public property during construction?

options.text: Lighting is required only during working hours when workers are present on site
Adequate lighting is required between sunset and sunrise
Lighting is required only at access points and gates
No specific lighting requirement is mandated by Section 1101

questions.rationale: The sunset-to-sunrise lighting requirement is absolute and applies to all temporary structures — not discretionary based on perceived pedestrian traffic volume. This protects both pedestrians and the contractor from liability.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Section 1106, what is the minimum height of a fence required to enclose a construction site adjacent to a public way, and on which side of the walkway must it be placed?

options.text: 2.40 m above grade; placed on the street side of the walkway, ensuring pedestrian safety
2.40 m above grade; placed on the construction side of the walkway nearest the building site
1.80 m above grade; placed on the street side of the walkway, providing a visual barrier
3.00 m above grade; placed on the construction side of the walkway nearest the building site, offering enhanced security

questions.rationale: The fence placement logic is intuitive once understood: the fence protects pedestrians from the construction site, so it goes on the side nearest the construction. The 2.40 m height corresponds to approximately one full storey — high enough to block visual access and contain small debris.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Section 1107, what are the contractor's obligations regarding pedestrian protection structures throughout the construction period?

options.text: Structures must be erected before construction begins and removed upon completion; no ongoing maintenance obligation is specified
Structures must be maintained in good condition throughout construction and removed upon completion of work
Structures may be removed and reinstalled as needed depending on the phase of construction
Maintenance is required only if the Building Official issues a specific maintenance order

questions.rationale: The continuing maintenance obligation connects to the permit system: temporary structures were placed under a special permit, and their maintenance throughout the project is a permit compliance condition. This is distinct from — and additional to — any BO enforcement order.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Section 1104, what obligation does the contractor have regarding utilities during construction, and what does this cover?

options.text: Utilities must be protected from damage only if they are located within the property boundary, and this includes both temporary and permanent installations
All public or private utilities above or below ground shall be protected from damage by work under the permit
The contractor is responsible only for underground utilities that have been previously surveyed and marked, ensuring no disruption to existing services
Utilities protection is required only for electrical and water supply lines, excluding other types of utilities such as gas or telecommunications

questions.rationale: The phrase 'above or below ground' covers both overhead hazards (crane booms near power lines) and subsurface hazards (excavation near water mains or telecom cables). The universal scope of 'all public or private utilities' prevents contractors from limiting their survey obligations.

questions.text: Per the mnemonic 'DT-CAR-SI' for Rule XV, Sec. 1501, what do the letters represent?

options.text: Definition, Testing, Connections, Anchorage, Rain protection, Safety, Inspection
Definition, Testing, Connections, Anchorage, Removed material allowances, Safety, Inspection
Design, Testing, Connections, Anchorage, Reinforcement, Safety, Installation
Definition, Thickness, Connections, Anchorage, Ratings, Standards, Inspection

questions.rationale: DT-CAR-SI stands for: D = Definition (structural unit assembled prior to incorporation), T = Testing (5 parameters by accredited labs), C = Connections (develop full member strength as integral structure), A = Anchorage (all probable external and internal forces), R = Removed material (allowances for pipes, conduits, equipment), S = Safety Engineer (required on site during placement — IRR only), I = Inspection (placement inspected for Code compliance — IRR only).

questions.text: Per PD 1096, Rule IX, Sec. 904, what is the critical prohibition regarding storm water and sanitary sewer systems?

options.text: Storm water may be combined with sanitary sewer only in sprinklered buildings
Rainwater drainage shall NOT discharge to the sanitary sewer system
Storm water may be discharged to sanitary sewer if capacity is certified by a licensed engineer
Combined sewers are permitted in industrial areas only

questions.rationale: Per Rule IX, Sec. 904, rainwater drainage shall NOT discharge to the sanitary sewer system. This prohibition is absolute. Combined sewers cause hydraulic overload (10–100× normal flow during rain events) and contamination. In typhoon-prone Philippines, this prevents leptospirosis and flooding risks.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Sec. 1102, which of the following items MUST NOT be blocked or obstructed by construction operations?

options.text: Street parking spaces, vendor stalls, and sidewalk cafes adjacent to the site
Fire hydrants, fire alarm boxes, utility access boxes, catch basins, and manholes
Pedestrian crossings, bus stops, and public benches within 50 m of the site
Street lighting fixtures, traffic signals, and road name signs

questions.rationale: Sec. 1102 explicitly prohibits blocking fire hydrants, fire alarm boxes, utility access boxes, catch basins, and manholes. These elements serve emergency response and public utility functions — obstruction can prevent firefighting access or cause flooding and utility failures during construction.
questions.explanation: The Sec. 1102 list is specific: fire hydrants, fire alarm boxes, utility access boxes, catch basins, manholes. Memorize the five categories. Street furniture, parking, and traffic signals are not in the Code's enumerated list.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Sec. 1101, what authorization is required before construction work can begin, and what lighting obligation applies to the site?

options.text: A contractor's bond is required; lighting is only required when work extends past midnight
Building Official authorization is required; the site must be illuminated from sunset to sunrise
DPWH clearance is required; lighting is only required when the site is adjacent to a national road
Barangay clearance is required; lighting must meet a minimum of 50 lux at all site boundaries

questions.rationale: Sec. 1101 requires Building Official authorization before commencing construction work, and mandates that the site be illuminated from sunset to sunrise. The sunset-to-sunrise requirement is absolute — it is not conditioned on road type, proximity, or work schedule.
questions.explanation: The paired requirements — BO authorization + sunset-to-sunrise lighting — are the baseline obligations of Sec. 1101. Both are frequently tested on the LEA as a single question covering the section's two mandates.

questions.text: A contractor argues that pedestrian protection measures can be removed once the structural frame is complete, while interior finishes continue. Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Sec. 1107, is this correct?

options.text: Yes; pedestrian protection applies only during the structural phase when falling materials are a risk, and not during interior work
No; Sec. 1107 requires all pedestrian protection measures to be maintained throughout construction and removed only upon completion of the work
Yes; interior work does not generate falling materials, so the walkway and fence can be removed after the frame is sealed, provided no exterior work is ongoing
No; but the walkway can be removed while the fence must remain until a Certificate of Occupancy is issued, ensuring safety compliance

questions.rationale: Sec. 1107 requires all pedestrian protection measures to be maintained throughout the entire construction period and removed only upon completion. Interior finishes still involve material deliveries, worker traffic, and potential falling tools or materials. The Code does not allow staged removal of protection measures during active construction.
questions.explanation: Sec. 1107 is a duration rule: protection measures persist throughout the project, not just during the structural phase. The LEA frequently tests whether candidates understand this continuity requirement versus the completion-triggered removal rule.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Sec. 1108, what permit is required for a demolition project, and why is it distinct from a building permit?

options.text: A standard building permit covers demolition; no separate permit is needed if the lot will be redeveloped, which simplifies the process
A separate demolition permit is required; demolition presents distinct structural, safety, and utility hazards not covered by building permits
A clearance from the DPWH is the only document needed since demolition affects public infrastructure, ensuring compliance
Barangay clearance is sufficient for structures under three storeys; full demolition permits only apply to buildings above 10 m, reducing bureaucracy

questions.rationale: Sec. 1108 explicitly establishes that demolition work requires a separate demolition permit, distinct from a building permit. Demolition involves progressive structural destabilization, hazardous material disturbance (asbestos, lead paint), staged utility disconnections, and debris management — hazards not present in new construction and therefore requiring dedicated regulatory oversight.
questions.explanation: The separate demolition permit requirement is a stand-alone rule in Sec. 1108. On the LEA, distractor options often suggest that a building permit covers demolition or that smaller structures are exempt — both are wrong under the Code.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Sec. 1103, what activity is ABSOLUTELY PROHIBITED on public streets during construction?

options.text: Delivery of building materials to the site during peak traffic hours
Mixing of mortar or concrete on any street or sidewalk surface
Storage of scaffolding materials on sidewalks for more than 24 hours
Use of pneumatic tools within 30 m of a residential structure

questions.rationale: Sec. 1103 absolutely prohibits the mixing of mortar or concrete on any street or public sidewalk. The word 'absolutely' in the Code is deliberate — there is no exception, no permit waiver, and no time-of-day exception. Mixing on streets causes surface damage, chemical contamination of stormwater drains, and pedestrian slip hazards.
questions.explanation: The absolute prohibition on street/sidewalk mixing is a bright-line rule. On the LEA, questions testing Sec. 1103 often include a scenario where the prohibition would seem inconvenient — the answer remains 'no, absolutely prohibited' regardless of circumstances.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Sec. 1105, what are the minimum width and required structural live load capacity of a pedestrian walkway provided alongside a construction site?

options.text: Minimum width 0.90 m; live load capacity of 480 kg/sq.m
Minimum width 1.20 m; live load capacity of 650 kg/sq.m
Minimum width 1.50 m; live load capacity of 480 kg/sq.m
Minimum width 1.00 m; live load capacity of 500 kg/sq.m

questions.rationale: Sec. 1105 requires the pedestrian walkway to be at least 1.20 m wide and structurally capable of supporting a live load of 650 kg/sq.m. The 650 kg/sq.m capacity accounts for crowd loading during emergency conditions when multiple pedestrians may simultaneously occupy the walkway. The walkway must also have a durable wearing surface.
questions.explanation: The paired values — 1.20 m width and 650 kg/sq.m live load — are the two quantitative requirements of Sec. 1105. The 1.20 m minimum matches the light/ventilation court passage minimum, which reinforces the value. The 650 kg/sq.m is substantially higher than normal pedestrian live loads (approximately 479 kg/sq.m) reflecting a safety margin.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Sec. 1106, when materials are stored on top of a construction canopy, what two additional features are specifically required?

options.text: A 300 mm curb board around the perimeter and a minimum 2.40 m clear height below the canopy
A 150 mm curb board around the perimeter and a minimum 3.00 m clear height below the canopy
Steel mesh netting over the canopy surface and a minimum 2.40 m clear height below the canopy
A 600 mm parapet wall around the canopy perimeter and a minimum 2.00 m clear height below the canopy

questions.rationale: Sec. 1106 requires: (1) a curb board at least 300 mm high along all open sides of the canopy when materials are stored on top, and (2) a minimum 2.40 m clear height beneath the canopy for pedestrian passage. The curb board prevents materials from rolling or being kicked off the canopy edge. The 2.40 m clear height ensures normal pedestrian passage including cyclists and taller individuals.
questions.explanation: The 300 mm curb board and 2.40 m clear height are the two quantitative requirements that apply specifically when materials are stored on the canopy. Without storage, the curb board is not required. Both values appear on the LEA as paired recall items.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Sec. 1106, what is the minimum height of the construction fence on the construction side of a pedestrian walkway, and what must it enclose?

options.text: 1.80 m above grade; must enclose only the active construction face of the building
2.40 m above grade; must enclose the entire construction site perimeter
1.50 m above grade; must enclose only the materials storage area
2.40 m above grade; must enclose only the demolition zone within the site

questions.rationale: Sec. 1106 requires the construction fence to be at least 2.40 m above grade and to enclose the entire construction site — not just one face or zone. The full-perimeter enclosure prevents unauthorized access from any direction and contains debris, dust, and hazardous materials within the site boundary.
questions.explanation: The 2.40 m height is the same as the canopy clear height, which helps memory by association. The 'entire site' requirement is the commonly missed detail — partial fencing that exposes rear or side property lines is non-compliant.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Sec. 1106, what is the height of the railing required along the outer edge of the pedestrian walkway separating it from vehicular traffic?

options.text: 0.75 m — the standard residential balcony guardrail height
1.00 m — the Code-prescribed walkway railing height under Sec. 1106
1.10 m — consistent with the corridor minimum width requirement
1.20 m — matching the minimum clear width of the walkway itself

questions.rationale: Sec. 1106 requires the railing on the traffic side of the pedestrian walkway to be 1.00 m high. This is a distinct value from the 0.75 m residential stair railing and the 1.10 m corridor width. The 1.00 m railing height provides a barrier that is visible to vehicle drivers and provides a graspable surface for pedestrians.
questions.explanation: The 1.00 m walkway railing is a third distinct height value alongside the 1.20 m walkway width and the 2.40 m fence height. These three quantities from Sec. 1106 are frequently tested as a set to probe which value applies to which element.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XI, Sec. 1104, which element must be protected when construction work is performed above ground utilities or below underground utilities?

options.text: Only overhead electrical lines within 3.00 m of the construction crane swing radius
All utilities — whether above or below ground — must be protected during construction
Only underground water supply and sewer lines; electrical utilities are managed by MERALCO separately
Only utilities owned by the government; private utility connections on the lot are the contractor's sole responsibility

questions.rationale: Sec. 1104 requires that all utilities — both above-ground and underground — be protected during construction. The section draws no distinction between utility types or ownership. Damage to any utility creates public safety hazards (electrocution, flooding, fire, loss of emergency services) and is the construction operator's responsibility to prevent.
questions.explanation: The broad scope of Sec. 1104 — all utilities, above and below ground — is the key fact. LEA distractors typically try to limit the provision to a specific utility type or ownership category. The Code is intentionally comprehensive.
